The video opens with three men in military uniforms working on the exterior of a gray fighter jet inside a hangar, one on a ladder and two others working at ground level. A close-up features one of the men in uniform, wearing earmuffs, as he tightens a screw on the exterior of the jet. Another man in uniform climbs into the cockpit. Next, a white round robot vacuum moves across a carpet; text overlaid on the video reads “the problems with AESA.” An F-35 jet is seen flying, followed by a propeller plane against a cloudy sky. Moving to an indoor setting, a man with short dark hair and a goatee is speaking to the camera with bookshelves filled with books in the background. Overlaid on the video, the word “OBSOLETE” appears in yellow letters with a picture of a radar; next a newspaper clipping featuring the title, "Northrop to produce new AN/APG-85 AESA radar for F-35 jets" is presented. The speaker emphasizes the importance of AESA radar, and in the next frame, the word “AESA” is in bold letters. He continues speaking, describing problems, and the terms “PESA”, “PEZA/AESA hybrids,” and “barely adequate” appear. The video cuts to a shot of an air force plane with radar equipment. It cuts back to the man speaking inside and then transitions to a scene of feet wearing festive socks in front of a fireplace. A woman in blue stands next to a large radar installation, smiling and pointing at it. Back to the man, speaking, and gesturing, as he mentions “some problems”; “Drawback” and “Don’t” are displayed in text. Finally, an F-35 fighter jet takes off from a ship at sea.
